content:
XL Games, the South Korean studio behind ArcheAge Chronicles, is planning a major restructuring and has not ruled out closing altogether after the game failed to meet sales expectations.
As reported by Korean outlet Money Today Broadcasting (MTN), translated by machine, CEO Choi Kwan-ho told staff in a letter on 26th November that the company would first ask for voluntary redundancies before moving on to compulsory layoffs.
"Criticisms regarding ArcheAge Chronicles' lack of polish despite its long development period, as well as complaints concerning bugs, gameplay, and optimisation, continue to persist," Choi wrote, according to MTN. "Sales are also showing a downward trend, and we anticipate revenue that will fall far short of expectations."
Choi said XL Games will try to address some of those problems in a December update, to see whether that turns things around.
"However, the company is currently at a critical crossroads where we must even consider the possibility of going out of business," he added.
To keep the company afloat, Choi said XL Games would need to "drastically" cut back its operations and focus on essential functions with a minimal workforce. He also promised to do everything possible to make sure staff leaving the company receive their severance pay and benefits, despite the "immense financial pressure" the studio is under.
ArcheAge Chronicles launched on 3rd November, 13 years after the original ArcheAge, and is described as a seamless open-world sandbox action RPG. According to MTN, it had a production budget of around £57 million (100 billion won), and sold roughly 100,000 copies in its first 10 days. That works out to about £2.3 million (4 billion won) in gross revenue before Steam's cut, which MTN says isn't enough to sustain the studio.
It currently has a "mixed" user score, with players complaining about the combat, the speed (or lack thereof) of upgrading, lack of polish, and QoL issues. Players were also incredibly unhappy that a pre-order bonus costume was only available for one character.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, the game had a troubled development. XL Games founder Song Jae-kyung - who previously led production at NCSoft and created the original ArcheAge - left the studio partway through, and the project changed direction several times.
